title: Course Schedule IV
summary: An edge [a,b] means course a must precede b.

contractDetails.constraints: 2–100 zero-based course labels. Prerequisite pairs are distinct, connect different courses, and form an acyclic graph. There are at most n(n−1)/2 prerequisite pairs and 1–10000 queries with distinct endpoints within each query.
contractDetails.output-checking: Return query-ordered integer flags, a lossless 0/1 projection of booleans. Prerequisite edges point from the earlier course to the later course.

statement: An edge [a,b] means course a must precede b. For each query [u,v], decide whether a chain of one or more prerequisite edges leads from u to v. Return the flags in query order, using 1 for yes and 0 for no.

examples.explanation: Reachability follows the edge direction and includes multi-edge paths.
The direct relationship works in one direction only.

constraints: 2–100 zero-based course labels. Prerequisite pairs are distinct, connect different courses, and form an acyclic graph. There are at most n(n−1)/2 prerequisite pairs and 1–10000 queries with distinct endpoints within each query.
hints: Conceptual: A prerequisite may be indirect.
Directional: Store whether each ordered pair is reachable.
Implementation: For each possible intermediate course k, update u→v when both u→k and k→v are already reachable.
complexityAnalysis: O(n³+q) time and O(n²) auxiliary space.
